title: Distilled language models retained a watermark-linked weight signal
summary: In controlled comparisons of models trained on matching clean or watermarked examples, researchers measured a watermark-linked component in the distilled models’ parameter changes. Its detectable signature persisted across some later model modifications tested in the study.
ai_technology: Fine-tuned Qwen language models; learned Qwen2.5-3B measurement probe

source_review.scope: §§2.2 and 3.1–3.3, matched-model geometry and aggregate validation limits

evidence.tested: The main comparison held the training task, prompts, initialization and recipe fixed between the clean and watermarked models. The authors measured changes in weights separately from output-level detections.
evidence.unknown: The represented observation is limited to tested models, watermark schemes and math distillation settings. The measured component is defined relative to a paired task-only change.
evidence.ai_role: Matched learned student models allowed the authors to isolate a component of weight change associated with the watermark without changing the training task.
